terms.gloss: a choice, the right or chance to choose; an option
evidence: Plaut. Cas. 292: optiō haec tua est
Cic. Fin. 1.33: cum solūta nōbīs est ēligendī optiō
Traupman 290: the choice is yours, optiō tua est
terms.comment: Optiō tua est or optiō sit tua (Cic. Fat. 3), it’s your choice, it’s up to you; potestātem optiōnemque facere, to give someone the choice (Cic. Div. Caec. 45, Lewis & Short). The masculine optiō is a soldier’s adjutant, another word.

phrases.latin: optiō haec tua est: utram hārum vīs condiciōnem accipe
phrases.english: the choice is yours: take whichever of these terms you like

phrases.latin: cum solūta nōbīs est ēligendī optiō, cumque nihil impedit, quō minus id, quod maximē placeat, facere possīmus
phrases.english: when our choice is free and nothing prevents us from doing what we like best

phrases.latin: hodiē, utrō fruī mālīs, optiō sit tua
phrases.english: today the choice is yours: which of the two would you rather enjoy?

sources: Lewis & Short: optio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 290.
